messages:
aj_support: Received an escalation from Acme Corp — invoice jumped ~3.2M tokens this billing period vs their SDK estimates. Customer says their client shows ~1.1M tokens. Requesting quick triage.

lina_billing: Oof. Do we have the customer id + any sample request ids?

aj_support: customer: acme-corp-001, billing period: feb 1-28. They attached a curl they used and a trace id: trace_8a7c. They also say this happens only for chat-style requests with tool calls.

sam_m: Common cause: server-side injected system/tool messages (moderation, analytics, routing sidecars) that client-side estimators don't see. Can you ask for a raw request/response pair?

aj_support: Pasting their minimal repro curl they sent (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-2025","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are helpful."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this product spec."}],"tools":[{"name":"search","input":"spec docs"}]}'
```

lina_billing: That looks ordinary. But if a sidecar is inserting extra tool calls (or we expand system messages for compatibility), that would increase billed tokens.

repro-bot: I repro'd locally with the customer's payload. Server logs (trimmed):
```
[2025-02-10T15:03:21Z] TRACE trace_8a7c request received messages=2 tools=1
[2025-02-10T15:03:21Z] INFO trace_8a7c injected_messages=3 injection_source=router-sidecar
[2025-02-10T15:03:21Z] INFO trace_8a7c model_input_tokens=1840 model_output_tokens=420 total_billed_tokens=2260
```

repro-bot: Customer-side token estimator (they shared SDK logs): estimated_input=600 estimated_output=380 total=980.

sam_m: Yep — router-sidecar is injecting 3 messages (analytics + provenance header messages + opt-in moderation stub) before serving. Those are included in model_input_tokens and thus appear on billing but not in client estimator.

jay_infra: Which code path injects those? I think we recently rolled a change to attach provenance footprints for private deployments.

repro-bot: I pulled the exact injection snippet from the infra logs:
```
// router-sidecar pseudolog
injected_messages: [
  {role: "system", content: "source: redwood-router v1.9"},
  {role: "tool", content: "moderation-check: pass"},
  {role: "system", content: "analytics: session=xyz"}
]
```

lina_billing: That explains spike. For this customer the sidecar was enabled for all requests (they're on Dedicated? yes). Need to quantify how many tokens those injected messages added over the period.

sam_m: Quick calculation: reproduction showed injected 3 messages => ~860 extra input tokens per request. Multiply by number of requests in period (customer reported ~3700 requests) => ~3.18M extra tokens. Matches invoice delta.

aj_support: Proposed mitigation and remediation? Customer wants credit or adjustment and a permanent fix so client estimates match billed counts.

jay_infra: Short term: offer a billing credit while we root cause and push a toggle to opt-out of router-sidecar injection for this customer. Long term: two action items: (1) ensure SDK estimator docs mention server-side injected tokens and provide a header to surface injected token counts, (2) add a metering header in server responses: X-RW-Injected-Token-Count so clients can reconcile.

sam_m: Also update our SDK estimator to optionally call /v1/debug/tokens?trace_id=... to fetch the full token breakdown (including injected messages and tool call tokens).

lina_billing: I'll draft the customer-facing note and create a credit for the delta pending engineering follow-up.

aj_support: Customer asked for repro steps so they can verify. Please post exact curl and expected debug header we will add.

repro-bot: Repro steps (do these on a non-prod tenant):
1) POST the customer's payload with header: `X-Debug-Trace: trace_8a7c`
2) check logs on router-sidecar: `kubectl logs router-sidecar-... | grep trace_8a7c`
3) call GET /v1/debug/tokens?trace_id=trace_8a7c to retrieve breakdown (will be added as internal debug endpoint).

Example server response (will include new header):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RW-Injected-Token-Count: 860
X-RW-Total-Model-Tokens: 2260
{
  "model_input_tokens": 1840,
  "model_output_tokens": 420,
  "injected_tokens": 860,
  "notes": "3 injected messages from router-sidecar"
}
```

lina_billing: Once engineering confirms counts we can proceed with a one-off invoice reconciliation for acme-corp-001.

sam_m: I'll open an internal bug (ENG-6528) to: disable router injection by default for Dedicated customers, add X-RW-Injected-Token-Count header, add docs on estimator differences, and extend SDK to fetch full token breakdown.

aj_support: Thanks — please tag me on the bug and I'll keep the customer updated.

lina_billing: I applied a provisional credit and emailed Acme finance. Customer replied with :relieved:.

jay_infra: Patch queued for rollout to staging tonight that adds the header. Will post deploy notifications.

sam_m: TL;DR: invoice spike caused by server-side injected system/tool messages (router-sidecar). Billing and estimator discrepancy expected behavior unless we surface injected tokens to clients.

aj_support: Good work team, keeping customer in the loop. Closing loop when ENG-6528 merged. :thumbsup:
